entries.title: Manage your Elastic security stack as code with the Elastic Stack Terraform provider
entries.description: From detection rules to AI connectors - the latest Terraform provider releases bring security, observability, and ML capabilities to your infrastructure-as-code workflows.

entries.title: Why 2026 is the Year to Upgrade to an Agentic AI SOC
entries.description: Agentic AI SOCs differ from copilot-only models by autonomously prioritizing attacks over alerts, executing closed-loop containment, and providing traceable reasoning for every decision, allowing analysts to focus on high-value investigations.

entries.title: Make The Most of Network Firewall Logs with Elastic Security
entries.description: Make the most of your firewall logs. In Part 1 of our series, learn how to ingest and parse logs from any firewall with Elastic Agent and use the Network Page to visually explore your network traffic for instant insights.

entries.title: Beyond Behaviors: AI-Augmented Detection Engineering with ES|QL COMPLETION
entries.description: Learn how Elastic's ES|QL COMPLETION command brings LLM reasoning directly into detection rules, enabling detection engineers to build intelligent alert triage without external orchestration.

entries.title: MIMICRAT: ClickFix Campaign Delivers Custom RAT via Compromised Legitimate Websites
entries.description: Elastic Security Labs uncovered a ClickFix campaign using compromised legitimate sites to deliver a five-stage chain ending in MIMICRAT, a custom native C RAT with malleable C2, token theft, and SOCKS5 tunneling.

entries.title: The Immutable Illusion: Pwning Your Kernel with Cloud Files
entries.description: Threat actors can abuse a class of vulnerabilities to bypass security restrictions and break trust chains.

entries.title: Speeding APT Attack Confirmation with Attack Discovery, Workflows, and Agent Builder
entries.description: This article walks through how Elastic Security's Attack Discovery, combined with Workflows and Agent Builder, can automatically detect, correlate, and confirm APT-level attacks like Chrysalis while reducing analyst response time from hours to minutes.

entries.title: BADIIS to the Bone: New Insights to a Global SEO Poisoning Campaign
entries.description: In November 2025, Elastic Security Labs observed an intrusion affecting a multinational organization based in Southeast Asia. During the analysis of this activity, our team observed various post-compromise techniques and tooling used to deploy BADIIS malware onto a Windows web server consistent with other industry publications.

entries.title: SolarWinds Web Help Desk Exploitation - February 2026
entries.description: Elastic Security detection and prevention capabilities for the recently-disclosed SolarWinds Web Help Desk vulnerabilities.

entries.title: DYNOWIPER: Destructive Malware Targeting Poland's Energy Sector
entries.description: Learn how Elastic Defend's ransomware protection successfully detects and prevents DYNOWIPER execution using canary file monitoring.

entries.title: Automating GOAD and Live Malware Labs
entries.description: Stop building labs by hand. Automate the deployment of a fully instrumented Purple Team range using Ludus and Elastic Security. Spin up infrastructure, execute attacks, and validate detection rules in a single, repeatable workflow.

entries.title: The Engineer's Guide to Elastic Detections as Code
entries.description: This post details the latest evolution of Elastic Security's Detections as Code (DaC) framework, including its development timeline, current feature highlights, and tailored implementation examples.

entries.title: From Alert Fatigue to Agentic Response: How Workflows and Agent Builder Close the Loop
entries.description: Attempting to chase individual alerts is a losing strategy. To succeed, we have to move beyond simple automation scripts and into the era of Agentic AI.

entries.title: From Qradar to Elastic: Automate your Detection Rule Migration
entries.description: Today, we are excited to announce a major expansion to our Automatic Migration feature that changes that narrative. In Elastic Security 9.3, we are introducing Automatic Migration support for QRadar detection rules (now in Tech Preview), joining our existing Splunk translation capabilities to further expedite your journey to Elastic Security. Let's take a closer look at what's supported.
